You asked for the dedup step now and tests afterwards, so I'll do that and leave the tests for the next pass. The TDD skill would normally have the failing test come first. You've made the call, so I won't hold it up.

The plan for `clean_sales()` in `pos/clean.py`:

- **Placement:** the step goes last, after the `sold_at` cast and the null `store_id` drop. It then compares real datetimes and doesn't spend work on rows that get dropped anyway.
- **Logic:** `.sort("sold_at").unique(subset=["store_id", "receipt_no"], keep="last", maintain_order=True)`. Sorting ascending and keeping the last row gives the latest `sold_at` per pair. Polars sorts nulls first by default, so a null `sold_at` loses to any real timestamp.
- **Tie-breaking:** if two rows share the same `sold_at`, the one later in the input wins, because the sort is stable.
- **Column names:** I'm assuming `store_id`, `receipt_no` and `sold_at` are the post-rename names. I'll confirm that when I re-read the file.

First I'll re-read the file for its exact text, then edit it, then run the existing suite to check nothing broke.
